ratio_note: ratio = rough native CPU time (user+sys) relative to the intended sol.cpp on the 'full' input: geometric mean of two check.py runs (best of 3 and best of 5), listed in ratio_runs, on one core of an Intel Xeon (Emerald Rapids, 2 MB L2, large shared L3) while other jobs ran on the remaining cores. Run-to-run spread is 10-30%, so treat it as a classification only.
too_slow_note: The variant with too_slow=true is meant to be rejected by any reasonable time limit (target 15-40x).

variants.name: queue_pair_vecvec
variants.description: Textbook BFS with std::queue<pair<int,int>> (deque) and vector<vector<int>> dist; no div/mod per pop.

variants.name: list_queue
variants.description: Queue is a std::list<pair<int,int>> (one heap node per cell) plus a bit-packed vector<vector<bool>> visited array.

variants.name: pq_instead_of_bfs
variants.description: Dijkstra with a binary heap of (dist,r,c) tuples on the unit-weight grid instead of a FIFO queue.

variants.name: bitset_frontier_sweep
variants.description: Bit-parallel BFS: every level recomputes the frontier for the whole grid with 64-bit word ops (~4000 full sweeps, no queue).

variants.name: unordered_map_dist
variants.description: Distances in an unordered_map<int,int> keyed by cell id (count + operator[] per neighbour) instead of a flat array.

variants.name: hash_seen_and_dist
variants.description: Two hash tables: unordered_set<long long> visited plus unordered_map<long long,int> dist, 64-bit keys.

variants.name: map_pair_dist
variants.description: TOO SLOW: std::map<pair<int,int>,int> distances, a red-black-tree walk over millions of nodes per lookup.

variants.name: bellman_ford_edges
variants.description: Bellman-Ford over the raw edge list with early exit: a few sequential passes over all edges with random dist reads/writes, no heap.

variants.name: vecvec_getchar_pq
variants.description: Same lazy binary-heap Dijkstra, but vector<vector<pair>> adjacency grown by push_back, vector<bool> done, getchar_unlocked reader.

variants.name: set_decrease_key
variants.description: std::set<pair<ll,int>> as an indexed priority queue (erase + reinsert on improvement), vector<vector<pair>> adjacency.

variants.name: scanf_vecvec_pq
variants.description: Standard lazy binary-heap Dijkstra with scanf input for all 1.8M numbers and vector<vector<pair>> adjacency.

variants.name: cin_synced
variants.description: The intended CSR + heap algorithm, but cin left synchronised with stdio (no sync_with_stdio(false)).

variants.name: map_adj_umap_dist
variants.description: std::map<int,vector<pair>> adjacency plus unordered_map dist and unordered_set done (tree + hash lookups instead of arrays).

variants.name: maps_everywhere_synced
variants.description: TOO SLOW: std::map adjacency, std::map dist, std::set done, std::set as the PQ, and cin synced with stdio.

variants.name: one_row_branchless
variants.description: Single DP row updated in place with a saved diagonal and branch-free max, scanf into char buffers.

variants.name: full_table_short
variants.description: Full (n+1)x(m+1) uint16_t table in one flat 128 MB array instead of two rolling rows (streaming writes).

variants.name: column_major_table
variants.description: Full vector<vector<uint16_t>> table filled column by column: the inner loop strides across 8000 rows (a new page per access).

variants.name: memo_recursion
variants.description: Top-down memoised recursion lcs(i,j) over a vector<vector<short>> memo (recursion depth up to n+m).

variants.name: hunt_szymanski
variants.description: Hunt-Szymanski: LIS over all ~16M matching (i,j) pairs, one lower_bound on the threshold vector per pair.

variants.name: lis_of_sorted_pairs
variants.description: Materialises all ~16M matching pairs in a vector, std::sorts them by (i asc, j desc), then patience-sorting LIS.

variants.name: hash_rows_copied
variants.description: TOO SLOW: each DP row is a fresh unordered_map<int,int> 'sparse array', copied into prev (prev = cur) every row.

variants.name: segtree_bottom_up
variants.description: Iterative bottom-up segment tree (2n array) with an fread reader and a hand-rolled integer writer.

variants.name: range_bit_template
variants.description: Generic range-add/range-sum two-BIT template used for point updates: O(n log n) build, both trees touched per operation.

variants.name: sqrt_decomposition
variants.description: Square-root decomposition: O(sqrt n) per query summing partial blocks element-wise and whole blocks via block sums.

variants.name: fenwick_cin_endl
variants.description: The intended Fenwick tree, but cin/cout (sync off) with endl after each answer: one write(2) per query.

variants.name: segtree_recursive
variants.description: Classic recursive top-down segment tree (4n array) with scanf input and a printf per answer.

variants.name: pointer_segtree
variants.description: Segment tree of heap-allocated nodes linked by pointers (new per node), cin input.

variants.name: map_fenwick
variants.description: TOO SLOW: the intended Fenwick tree stored in a std::map<int,long long> used as a sparse array.

variants.name: shift_and_bitap
variants.description: Shift-And (bitap): one shift/OR/AND per text character on a 64-bit state, KMP fallback for patterns longer than 64.

variants.name: kmp_automaton
variants.description: KMP compiled into a 256-column DFA: one dependent table load per character (no fallback loop); fread input.

variants.name: rolling_hash
variants.description: Rabin-Karp with a hash modulo 2^61-1 (128-bit multiplies), every hash hit confirmed with memcmp.

variants.name: z_function
variants.description: Z-function over pattern + '#' + text: a 20M-entry int array and a second pass to collect matches.

variants.name: kmp_cin_synced
variants.description: The intended KMP, but cin left synchronised with stdio, so the 20 MB text is read through stdio char by char.

variants.name: substr_compare
variants.description: Brute force with t.substr(i, m) == p at every position: one heap-allocated 24-char temporary per text position.

variants.name: hash_from_scratch
variants.description: TOO SLOW: 'Rabin-Karp' recomputing each window's hash mod 1e9+7 from scratch (O(n*m)), hits verified exactly.

variants.name: offline_two_pointer
variants.description: Offline: sort values and (query, index) pairs, two-pointer sweep, answers printed in input order with printf.

variants.name: merge_sort_vectors
variants.description: Hand-written recursive merge sort copying both halves into fresh vectors at every level, hand-written binary search, printf.

variants.name: list_sort
variants.description: Values in a std::list sorted with list::sort (merge sort over scattered nodes), copied to a vector for upper_bound.

variants.name: cin_endl
variants.description: Same sort + upper_bound with cin/cout (sync off) and endl after every answer: one write(2) per query.

variants.name: cin_synced
variants.description: Same sort + upper_bound with cin/cout left synchronised with stdio ('\n', no endl).

variants.name: pbds_order_tree
variants.description: __gnu_pbds order-statistics red-black tree over (value, index) pairs; order_of_key per query.

variants.name: sqrt_sorted_blocks
variants.description: TOO SLOW: sqrt-decomposition template with sorted blocks of size sqrt(n log n); each query binary-searches all ~160 blocks.

variants.name: bfs_order_reverse
variants.description: No DFS: BFS from the root records order/parents/depths, subtree sizes accumulated over the reversed order.

variants.name: stack_pairs_vecvec
variants.description: Iterative preorder with std::stack<pair<int,int>> over vector<vector<int>> adjacency, sizes summed in reverse preorder.

variants.name: vecvec_recursive_scanf
variants.description: Recursive DFS (depth 1e6) over vector<vector<int>> adjacency with scanf input.

variants.name: set_adjacency
variants.description: Recursive DFS over vector<set<int>> adjacency: every neighbour is a separately allocated tree node.

variants.name: umap_adjacency
variants.description: Recursive DFS over unordered_map<int, vector<int>> adjacency: a hash lookup plus a heap vector per vertex.

variants.name: multimap_adjacency
variants.description: Both edge directions in one std::multimap<int,int>; recursive DFS enumerates neighbours with equal_range (tree search per vertex).

variants.name: map_of_sets
variants.description: TOO SLOW: 'graph as a map of sets' (map<int,set<int>>), std::map of subtree sizes, recursive DFS, cin synced with stdio.
